items.title: Random errors on accessing cache with simultaneous installs on Windows
items.reason: Canonical open tracker for intermittent Windows failures during environment creation and installation, including Jenkins, the identical os error 33 text, retry success, shared-cache access, and antivirus discussion.

items.title: Concurrent cache access causes errors on Windows
items.reason: Contains the exact `RECORD file is invalid` Windows failure and was explicitly closed by a maintainer as a duplicate of astral-sh/uv#2810.

items.title: Guard against concurrent cache writes on Windows
items.reason: Historical fix adding locks around wheel extraction and cache writes for astral-sh/uv#11002. The exact failure was reproduced afterward, leaving the broader problem open.

items.title: Windows antivirus/EDR issues
items.reason: Current tracking resource for Windows AV/EDR interference and similar file-access errors. It matches the environment, although antivirus is not confirmed as the locking process.

items.title: Retry `PermissionDenied` errors on Windows in the request retry layer
items.reason: Proposes additional retries for AV/EDR-related Windows cache failures and cites astral-sh/uv#2810, but targets PermissionDenied/os error 5 rather than this RECORD-related os error 33 path.

related.search_scope: Literal searches covered `RECORD file is invalid`, `locked a portion of the file`, `os error 33`, Windows, venv, and wheel-install failures. Conceptual searches covered intermittent retry success, concurrent/shared cache writes, antivirus/EDR locking, access denied, sharing violations, cache persistence, and atomic replacement. Fix-oriented inspection covered merged astral-sh/uv#11007 and open astral-sh/uv#21489 and their linked discussions. astral-sh/uv#14345 was ruled out because it concerns deterministic malformed RECORD CSV on Linux. astral-sh/uv#2767 and astral-sh/uv#2800 were ruled out because they concern acquiring the virtual-environment `.lock`, not reading or installing RECORD/cache contents.

type_reason: The same intermittent Windows installation failure is already centralized in open astral-sh/uv#2810. Most decisively, astral-sh/uv#11002 records the exact `RECORD file is invalid` failure caused by another process using the file and was explicitly deduplicated into astral-sh/uv#2810. Although astral-sh/uv#11007 attempted a fix, the failure remained reproducible and the canonical tracker remains open. Antivirus is plausible given astral-sh/uv#20792 but is not confirmed here.
summary: Open astral-sh/uv#2810 is the canonical tracker. Closed astral-sh/uv#11002 supplies the exact RECORD-error precedent, while astral-sh/uv#11007 is the incomplete historical fix. astral-sh/uv#20792 and astral-sh/uv#21489 are relevant to the AV/EDR context but do not clearly cover this os error 33 path.
draft_response:
Thanks for the report. This matches the intermittent Windows file-locking failures tracked in astral-sh/uv#2810. In particular, the same `RECORD file is invalid` installation failure was reported in astral-sh/uv#11002, which was consolidated into that issue after it remained reproducible following astral-sh/uv#11007.

The antivirus/EDR context may be relevant and is tracked in astral-sh/uv#20792, but this error alone does not identify which process holds the lock. Please add any reliable reproduction details to astral-sh/uv#2810, especially whether the Jenkins jobs run concurrently or share a uv cache, and whether the failure still occurs with the current uv release. If your AV/EDR vendor is implicated, please also share the vendor and its support ticket ID as requested in astral-sh/uv#20792.
